issues.claim: "Обзор моделей хранилищ данных" / "Overview of data store models"
issues.problem: The link redirects to a page titled 'Understand Data Models' (/azure/architecture/data-guide/technology-choices/understand-data-store-models). The link title is a paraphrase and does not match the real page title. The page itself supports the relational vs nonrelational trade-offs: ACID transactions and joins on the relational side, flexible schema on the nonrelational side.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the URL to the canonical https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/data-guide/technology-choices/understand-data-store-models. Retitle to 'Understand data models' (en) and 'Основные сведения о моделях данных' (ru).

issues.claim: in Cosmos DB it cannot be changed on an existing container, you need a new container and a data migration
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of the partitioning page does not show this immutability claim. From my own knowledge it is correct: Cosmos DB's change-partition-key feature works by container copy into a new container. The 'single logical partition' transaction scope is supported by the excerpt ('A logical partition also defines the scope of database transactions').
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the claim. Optionally rephrase to 'cannot be changed in place; changing it means copying the data into a new container with the new key', and consider citing the Cosmos DB change-partition-key / container copy docs.

issues.claim: доступ к данным за границей модуля
issues.problem: In Russian, 'за границей' reads as 'abroad'. The English text says 'behind a module boundary'.
issues.suggestedFix: доступ к данным за интерфейсом модуля (или: за границей модуля - 'за границами модуля').

issues.claim: For a relational database the schema changes through migrations, which is reversible
issues.problem: Migrations are not always cleanly reversible, for example when columns are dropped or data is transformed. 'Reversible' slightly overstates this.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'which is usually manageable and mostly reversible'.

issues.claim: Start not with the technology but with which reads and writes the service will do most often and which data must change atomically together.
issues.problem: The hint effectively states the answer's central thesis (access patterns drive the choice). It is still a nudge and not a full answer.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it, for example: 'What do you need to know about how the data will be used before comparing the technologies?'
